override.reason: Daemon review ran six rounds in two cycles (cycle 1: 6 MED; 1 HIGH + 3 MED; 4 MED. Cycle 2: 2 MED; 1 MED; 2 MED) and never returned a clean verdict. Every finding was fixed in the LLD except DEF s3 ac6, which needs a DEF amendment the amendment tool cannot file (HLD-only); the ac6 reading and the final round's retire-permissions.mode test and fixture sites are recorded in docs/plans/tool-registry.md. AMD-4 to AMD-7 are prerequisites for the s2 and s3 plans. User approved with override.

summary.prose: This Story replaces the executor's 'auto-approving' fallback with a daemon-owned approval broker. A tool declares one approval class (none, common or destructive); a destructive call always asks the user, a common call follows the global setting or the chat's edits mode, and a call nobody answers is denied. Clients (terminal client, editor, chat) open an approval stream, show the exact call and answer over one RPC.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a1: the executor in src/daemon/tools/executor.ts becomes the one pipeline for all external operations, and git, gh and Jira (acli) are registry tool families with an optional declared output schema and an approval class (none, common or destructive). Workflow and daemon code call tools through a typed helper that takes the tool definition; about 32 production files that spawn git or gh, or call a wrapper that does, move onto it in one change.

ownedContracts.name: Approval class and approval exchange
ownedContracts.purpose: Defines the one field that gives a tool or call its approval class, the global setting that governs the common class, the request the executor sends to the attached client, the answer, the timeout and the denial reasons, so that every client implements the same exchange.

boundary.internal: The approval step at step 2 of the pipeline: the single approval field on a tool definition, the global approval setting for the common class and its default, the IPC request and answer methods, the timeout value, the daemon-side holder of the pending requests, the terminal-client, editor and chat implementations of the answer, and removal of the 'auto-approving' fallback in executor.ts. It maps every existing requiresApproval flag, in every family, to the common class, and lists the tools that change. It does not choose which individual git, gh or Jira operations are destructive; each family Story marks its own.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The hook stage inside executeTool: the registry of hooks keyed by tool id, registration order, the rule that a hook runs only after a successful, checked call, and the way a hook failure is carried on the result. It places its stage at step 5 of the pipeline order in the architecture shape and does not own the schema check or the approval step.

The optional output-schema field and the check at step 4 of the pipeline, the typed call helper that takes a tool definition, the serial conversion queue, the key-value cross-check and the one-time escalation, and the shared failure kinds. It includes the choice of schema language and the way an input-to-tool mismatch is reported. It does not declare or read the approval class.

The list of git operation families, their input and output schemas, which git operations are in the destructive class (for example force push, hard reset, clean, deleting a branch or tag), and the parsing of git porcelain output. Operations that need approval but cannot destroy work stay in the common class. Existing git ids keep their meaning.

The list of gh operation families, their schemas (read from gh --json where it exists, converted from text otherwise, for example gh pr diff and gh run view --log), which of the 27 gh operations that need approval are in the destructive class, and the 120 second time limit and its message. Existing gh ids keep their meaning.

The Jira tool families over acli (work item view, search, create, edit, transition, assign, comment, link, project list and view), their schemas, the --yes flag on every mutating command, the bounded forms of search and project list that acli requires, the 'acli jira auth status' sign-in check, and which operations are in the destructive class. An operation acli does not offer is left out and named as unsupported.

The repository check that fails on a direct git, gh or acli spawn outside src/daemon/tools, built first; the inventory it produces (about 32 production files known today, with the indexer, the design corpus reader, the analyze ignore filter, the understanding identity lookup and the daemon self-update included and no allowlist); the rewrite of every listed site and of the tests that import the old wrappers onto the typed helper; and the removal of runGit, commitAndPushArtifacts and the github.ts wrappers. It keeps the artifacts, commits and tracker records the same as before.

nonFunctional.performance: gh commands time out after 120 seconds (decided with the user; the daemon is expected to become multi-threaded so a slow gh will not block it). The approval wait has its own timeout, set in s3's LLD. Conversion is serial, so a text-only tool that needs the cheap model costs one model call per attempt plus at most one escalated call; structured-output tools make no model call.
nonFunctional.security: No argument, setting, environment variable or caller identity can skip the approval for a destructive call; with no client attached the call is denied. Common calls follow one global setting. Approval requests travel only over the daemon's Unix socket. No credentials are read or stored: gh, git and acli use the user's own CLI sessions. A tool that declares an output schema and returns a result that does not match it fails and its result is not passed on. Today the executor runs every tool flagged requiresApproval as approved (11 git tools, 5 more by predicate, 27 gh operations and other families), so nothing asks; this Epic makes destructive calls ask every time and puts the rest under the global setting.
nonFunctional.observability: The executor logs each stage per call with the tool id, the caller, the approval class and decision and its reason, the schema check result, and each hook outcome. Hook failures, denials and conversion escalations are returned to the caller as part of the result, not only logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Pending approval requests are held in memory by the daemon and are lost on restart; a request left open at restart is treated as denied. Hooks are registered in code at start-up, not stored. The global approval setting is stored in the daemon's config. The cutover leaves artifacts, commits and tracker records unchanged.

parameters.name: req

dataModelChanges.details: New field on Tool replacing requiresApproval and destructive. Value is a class or a per-input function.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
- requiresApproval?: boolean | (input) => boolean
- destructive?: boolean
+ approval?: ApprovalClass | (input) => ApprovalClass

dataModelChanges.details: Adds caller ('agent' | 'daemon' | 'workflow') for logging and approvalMode ('manual' | 'edit-auto' | 'auto', optional) set by the entry point from the chat's edits mode; absent means the global flag. Neither is read for the destructive class. Of the four ToolDeps builders only src/analyze/context/driver.ts and src/agent/providers/ollama.ts reach executeTool; src/workflow/code-review/grounding.ts and src/workflow/runners/build/changed-files.ts call the read-only git_diff tool's execute directly, so no approval step runs for them and this field does not govern them until s7 moves them onto the typed helper.

Request carries requestId, toolId, approvalClass, repoPath (input cwd, else deps.repoPath), arguments, preview, reason, expiresAt. Answer carries requestId and decision. Denial is one of declined, timed-out, no-client, cancelled (the caller's signal aborted).

In-memory map of requestId to resolver and timer, plus the set of open approval streams. Lost on restart; open requests then count as denied. First answer wins. The wait ends 300 seconds after the request is raised (expiresAt); the value is a constant of the broker.

Global flag for the common class: manual, edit-auto or auto; default auto. It is an enum entry in the on-disk config catalog (src/config/config-catalog.ts), stored in ~/.insrc/config.json, so it survives a restart; the in-memory ToolSettings snapshot is not used for it, because it resets on restart and nothing sets it now that the IDE is deprecated. In src/daemon/tools/config.ts, approval.defaultAction and destructive.requireDoubleConfirm are read by nothing outside that file; they are removed, because a 'destructive' setting must not be able to alter the destructive path (ac5) and a second common-class setting would conflict with this one. The existing catalog entry permissions.mode ('validate' | 'auto-accept', config-catalog.ts, typed in src/shared/types.ts and surfaced as insrc.permissions.mode in vscode-plugin/package.json) is read by nothing at runtime. It is retired (added to RETIRED_PATHS so the boot reconcile strips it) and not migrated: its default 'validate' was never a user choice, and mapping it to manual would silently turn the confirmed default (auto) into manual. tools.commonApproval is the only tool-approval setting.

approval.subscribe is a stream handler pushing 'gate' frames to the client; approval.answer is a unary RPC carrying { requestId, decision }. Client side: a streaming method is added to IpcClient in src/shared/ipc-client.ts (the vscode-plugin reaches the daemon through that interface) as an optional member, so the IpcClient test doubles (vscode-plugin/src/config/__tests__/per-role-engine.test.ts, vscode-plugin/src/workspace/__tests__/registrar.test.ts, and the doubles in activation.test.ts and controller.test.ts) keep compiling and only the subscribing modules check for it; the terminal client subscribes from a service under src/cli/services; the editor and chat modules under vscode-plugin/src/chat and vscode-plugin/src/daemon subscribe, render and answer. src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts is only a model for the streaming client; the MCP process is a machine client and does not subscribe.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: s3 owns sc4: builds the class field, the global flag, ApprovalRequest/Answer/Denial, the broker, the timeout and the two IPC methods, and refines the sketch as in the amendment proposal. Carrier decision: the tool-call IPC that CLI-process and chat callers use is built by s7, but its request fields are defined here as part of sc4: caller ('agent' | 'daemon' | 'workflow') and an optional approvalMode ('manual' | 'edit-auto' | 'auto'); the daemon sets deps.caller and deps.approvalMode from them. This is a requirement on s7: build the method against these fields. A chat sends its session's PermissionMode as approvalMode on each such call. The chat does not call registry tools today, so ac6's chat clause is met at the client level (the chat opens approval.subscribe and answers) and for chat-originated calls once s7's method exists.

Returns denials as s2's ToolFailure with kind 'denied' and ToolDenialReason; adds caller and approvalMode to ToolDeps beside s2's conversion field. The value 'cancelled' (an aborted approval) is not in s2's ToolDenialReason: it is raised as amendment AMD-b7a68147dcf72034-5 on sc5, which must be approved before the s3 build.
Approval runs at step 2 before the hook stage at step 5; a denied call is not run and so fires no hook.

errorCases.scenario: No client has an open approval stream when a destructive call is made
errorCases.detection: The broker finds its set of open approval streams empty when ask() is called.
errorCases.response: ask() resolves 'no-client' at once; the executor returns a failed result with a denied ToolFailure (reason no-client) and the tool does not run.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller is told the call was denied because nobody could answer; nothing changes.

errorCases.scenario: A client is subscribed but does not answer before expiresAt
errorCases.detection: The per-request timer set at ask() fires while the request is still in the pending table.
errorCases.response: The request is removed, ask() resolves 'timed-out', the executor returns a denied failure (reason timed-out), and a late approval.answer is ignored.
errorCases.userImpact: The call fails with a lack-of-answer message; the user can repeat the call.

errorCases.detection: approval.answer arrives with decision 'decline' for a pending requestId.
errorCases.response: ask() resolves 'declined'; the executor returns a denied failure (reason declined); the tool does not run.
errorCases.userImpact: Nothing is changed; the caller sees the decline.

errorCases.scenario: approval.answer names an unknown, expired or already answered requestId
errorCases.detection: The pending-table lookup by requestId misses.
errorCases.response: The RPC returns { accepted: false } and logs at warn level; no pending request is affected.
errorCases.userImpact: The client shows that the request is no longer open.

errorCases.scenario: Every subscribed client disconnects while a request is pending
errorCases.detection: The server aborts each subscribe handler's signal when its socket closes; the broker sees the open-stream count reach zero.
errorCases.response: All pending requests resolve 'no-client' immediately rather than waiting for the timer.
errorCases.userImpact: Calls fail fast with a denial instead of hanging.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon restarts with requests pending
errorCases.detection: The pending table is in memory, so the old process's callers see their connection drop.
errorCases.response: Nothing is persisted and nothing is replayed; the interrupted call never ran.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller sees a connection error and starts again.

errorCases.scenario: The caller's signal aborts while a request is pending
errorCases.detection: deps.signal fires while ask() is waiting.
errorCases.response: The request is removed from the pending table and the subscribers receive a 'gate' cancel frame; ask() resolves 'cancelled' and the executor returns a denied failure with reason cancelled, and the tool does not run.
errorCases.userImpact: The prompt disappears from the client.

errorCases.scenario: The global setting holds an unknown value or the config cannot be read
errorCases.detection: The config reader validates the value against manual, edit-auto and auto.
errorCases.response: It falls back to the default 'auto' for common calls and logs a warning; the destructive class does not read the setting.
errorCases.userImpact: Common calls follow the default; destructive calls still ask.

errorCases.detection: The executor catches the rejection when building the preview.
errorCases.response: The request is sent with a generic preview (tool id, repository, arguments as JSON); the approval still happens.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees the raw call instead of a tailored preview.

errorCases.scenario: A tool's per-input approval function throws
errorCases.detection: The executor catches the exception when resolving the class.
errorCases.response: The class is treated as destructive (the safe side) and the failure is logged.

edgeCases.input: Two destructive calls are made at once from different callers
edgeCases.expected: Each gets its own requestId and its own prompt; answering one does not answer the other.

edgeCases.input: Two clients are subscribed and both answer
edgeCases.expected: The first answer wins; the second receives accepted: false.

edgeCases.input: A common-class tool called with deps.approvalMode 'auto' while the global flag is 'manual'
edgeCases.expected: The call mode wins; it does not ask.

edgeCases.input: A common-class tool called with no approvalMode and the global flag 'edit-auto'
A destructive tool called with approvalMode 'auto' or caller 'daemon'
edgeCases.expected: It asks; neither field is read for the destructive class.

edgeCases.input: A git tool called with no cwd in its input
edgeCases.expected: The request names deps.repoPath; if that is also empty the request says the repository is unknown.

edgeCases.input: A tool whose per-input approval function returns none for one input and destructive for another
edgeCases.expected: Each call is classed from its own input.

edgeCases.input: A client subscribes after the request was raised
edgeCases.expected: It receives the still-pending requests on subscribe, so a late client can answer them.

edgeCases.input: Arguments contain a very large value such as a file body
edgeCases.expected: The request carries arguments truncated for display with the full length noted; the executed call uses the untruncated input.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Tool ids and their input schemas do not change; only the approval field replaces requiresApproval and destructive.
The daemon owns all approval state and CLI, MCP and editor reach it only over the Unix-socket IPC.
executeTool still never throws: every failure returns a ToolResult with success false.
The daemon still never opens a connection to a client; it pushes only over a stream the client opened.

migration.stateBefore: executeTool in src/daemon/tools/executor.ts:41-48 treats requiresApproval (true or a predicate) as approved, logs 'auto-approving' and runs the tool, so nothing asks. Tool in src/daemon/tools/types.ts:110-128 has requiresApproval and destructive; eight builtins set destructive: true. ToolDeps (src/daemon/tools/types.ts:50-81) has no caller or approval-mode field. The IPC server can push to a client only over a stream the client opened (src/daemon/server.ts:242-290); IpcStreamKind already lists 'gate' but no handler uses it, and the gate.request-permission stream is an offline stub (src/daemon/index.ts:1923-1945).
migration.stateAfter: Tool declares one approval field (none, common or destructive, or a per-input function). executeTool resolves the class and, for destructive calls and for common calls whose effective mode is manual or edit-auto, asks the daemon-owned broker, which pushes the exact call to every client with an open approval.subscribe stream and waits for an approval.answer, a timeout or a disconnect. A call not approved returns a denied failure and does not run. The terminal client, the editor and a chat each implement the subscribe and answer. The common class follows tools.commonApproval (default auto) unless the call carries an approvalMode. The 'auto-approving' fallback, requiresApproval and destructive are gone.

migrationSteps.action: Add the ApprovalClass type, the optional approval field on Tool, and the optional caller and approvalMode fields on ToolDeps beside the old fields; nothing reads them yet.

Add the tools.commonApproval entry (enum manual, edit-auto, auto; default auto) to src/config/config-catalog.ts so it is stored in ~/.insrc/config.json, filled by the boot reconcile and read by the executor per call; remove the unread approval.defaultAction and destructive.requireDoubleConfirm from src/daemon/tools/config.ts so no second approval setting remains. Retire permissions.mode (unread) through RETIRED_PATHS in src/config/config-catalog.ts, and remove its insrc.permissions.mode contribution from vscode-plugin/package.json. Update the tests that assert the current state: the RETIRED_PATHS count test in src/config/__tests__/config-catalog-contract.test.ts (6 becomes 7), and the assertion in src/daemon/__tests__/config-boot-reconcile.test.ts that permissions.mode is 'validate' (it becomes: tools.commonApproval is 'auto' and permissions.mode is pruned). Drop permissions.mode from site/settings.html. Also update src/config/__tests__/config-reconcile-smoke.test.ts (the permissions assertion becomes: permissions is absent), the fixture src/config/__tests__/fixtures/daemon-defaults-literal.json (drop permissions.mode), and the note in src/config/__tests__/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md that names permissions.mode as surviving.
Add the approval broker and the approval.subscribe stream and approval.answer RPC to the daemon handler maps; no tool uses them yet. Keep the gate.request-permission stub as it is.

Add the client side: the terminal client, the editor and the chat open approval.subscribe, show the exact call and answer through approval.answer. Clients that connect before the executor change simply receive no frames.

Map every builtin: map requiresApproval true to approval 'common', a predicate to a per-input function returning common or none, and false or absent to none (the 77 requiresApproval: false declarations across 55 read-only tools just drop the field and stay at none), and replace the eight destructive: true builtins with approval 'destructive'; remove the old fields from every file in the same change, including src/docgen/tool.ts, the one Tool outside the builtins that declares requiresApproval.

Switch the executor to resolve the class and ask the broker; remove the 'auto-approving' branch; set caller at the two ToolDeps builders that reach executeTool (src/analyze/context/driver.ts and src/agent/providers/ollama.ts); the two direct-execute builders are left to s7. Remove requiresApproval and destructive from the Tool type.
Run the full test sweep once, then update docs/daemon.md with the approval exchange, the config key and the class mapping.

migration.backwardCompat: Tool ids and input schemas are unchanged. The Tool type loses requiresApproval and destructive; every use is in this repository's builtins and is changed in the same step, and the IDE repo is deprecated so no outside consumer exists. Behaviour changes on purpose: tools flagged requiresApproval now ask in manual and edit-auto, and the eight destructive builtins always ask; with no client attached a destructive call is denied where it used to run. Under the default auto mode common calls still run without asking, so existing unattended flows are unchanged except for destructive tools.

alternativesConsidered.name: A daemon-owned approval broker that human clients subscribe to
alternativesConsidered.summary: The daemon holds the pending requests and the timeout; any client that opens an approval stream receives each request and answers by one RPC; with no subscriber the call is denied.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask the client that started the call, over its own stream
alternativesConsidered.summary: The executor pushes the approval request as a frame on the originating request's stream and waits for an answer RPC; calls with no originating stream are denied.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Many callers have no human behind their stream (an MCP-driven workflow, daemon-internal work), so their destructive calls are denied even when a TUI is open; partial on ac1, ac6 and sc4.

alternativesConsidered.name: Hybrid: the originating client first, subscribers otherwise
alternativesConsidered.summary: The broker sends the request to the originating stream when its client has said it can answer approvals, and to the subscribers when it has not.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds a routing path and a caller-sent capability flag to a rule that must not depend on the caller; a silent client waits out the timeout; partial on ac5 and k5.

alternativesConsidered.name: A caller-supplied approval gate on ToolDeps
alternativesConsidered.summary: ToolDeps carries an ask function; whoever builds the deps supplies it, and the executor calls it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Any caller can pass a function that always approves and the ask never crosses the daemon's IPC; violates ac5, sc4, k4 and k5.

openQuestions: dm2 (partial): the dataModel entries do not each cite the invariant they might break; the invariant that tool ids and schemas stay unchanged is listed under invariantsToPreserve.
ep3 (partial): the invariants rest on direct code reads recorded in the s1 bundles, not on insrc_analyze_step output.

DEF reading for s3 ac6: 'a tool that needs approval asks when the effective mode says ask (manual, edit-auto), and a destructive tool always asks'; the amendment tool is HLD-only, so this is recorded here only.
Open design details left to the plan: the exact terminal-client and editor prompt UI, and whether the terminal client and editor open approval.subscribe at attach or on demand.

Amendments filed, pending the user's approval: AMD-b7a68147dcf72034-4 (sc4 request fields, three chat modes, approval.subscribe), -5 (sc5 'cancelled' denial reason), -6 (sc2 typebox outputSchema, TypedTool, callTool), -7 (sc3 convertText takes ToolDeps, keyValues required). -1 (superseded) and -2 (duplicate of -3) are to be rejected.
